solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique, linked answer split by the grid); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Miserable subsection of loathsome agreement

indicators.note: a subsection is a small part cut out of something, so the letters sit inside the words loathsome agreement

explanation.surface: Someone sour about a hateful deal they were forced into.
explanation.definitionFit: A miserable portion is a paltry, scanty one, the adjective's sense of poor in quantity.

clue.text: G type of oil burnt by late work

definitions.meaning: the letter G is the middle of the word night, so cryptically it is the dead centre of the night

definitions.text: type of oil burnt by late work
definitions.meaning: people working late into the night are said to burn this kind of oil

explanation.walkthrough: The lone letter G is a definition: it stands at the very middle of NIGHT, so it is cryptically the moment twelve hours after noon.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom burning the midnight oil means working late; G is the centre letter of night.

clue.text: Pride of farm crop, egg was once set to be shelled

indicators.note: shelling removes the outer casing, so each of the six words loses its first and last letter

explanation.surface: A farmer's pride in a crop and eggs that used to sell well.
explanation.definitionFit: Pride in the sense of haughty self-importance is a synonym for an overbearing manner.

clue.text: Famous person helps sailor to go to sleep

parts.note: helps someone to go to sleep, as a parent rocks a cradle; the phrase to go to sleep completes the sense
a tar is an old word for a seaman

explanation.surface: A celebrity lulling a seaman to sleep.
explanation.walkthrough: 'helps ... to go to sleep' is one idea: to rock a baby to sleep.
explanation.definitionFit: A celebrated pop musician is the archetypal famous person, so the phrase is used for any celebrity.

clue.text: About rent in arrears, perhaps to one's ears, a type of clue that's somewhat new

definitions.text: About rent in arrears, perhaps to one's ears, a type of clue that's somewhat new

indicators.note: about means going around, so the sound-alike word surrounds the backward rental
something heard by the ears is judged by its sound, so the word clue is replaced by a spelling that sounds the same

parts.note: clue taken as written, to be heard

indicators.note: in arrears means behind, so the word for rent is read from the back

parts.note: to rent is to hire

explanation.surface: A light verse joke about an unpaid rent bill, offered as a newish sort of clue.
explanation.walkthrough: The heard spelling is an old variant of clue, and 'in arrears' turns the rent word backwards before 'About' wraps it. The whole clue plays at being an example of the verse form.
explanation.definitionFit: This four-line comic verse, invented by E. C. Bentley around 1905, is a fairly recent form; the clue itself plays at being one.

clue.text: See friend set up computers

indicators.note: in a down clue, set up means raised upwards, so the letters read from bottom to top

parts.note: to see is to spot
a pal is a friend

explanation.surface: Watching a mate install some computers.
explanation.definitionFit: Portable machines that rest on the knees are a kind of personal computer.

clue.text: Where to find goods left in stricken pirate ship

indicators.note: a stricken vessel is wrecked, so the letters of pirate together with the extra letter are broken up

parts.note: the ark is Noah's ship

explanation.surface: Plunder stowed in a wrecked buccaneer vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' says the L goes among the letters of pirate before 'stricken' scrambles them into RETAILP.
explanation.definitionFit: An out-of-town shopping complex is a place where shops sell goods to the public.

clue.text: Difficulty with knot

definitions.meaning: a kind of knot used to fasten a rope to something

explanation.definitionFit: A snag in plans and a fastening of rope are both senses of the same word.

clue.text: Freak party under waterfall

indicators.note: in a down answer, under places the second piece below the first

parts.note: a weir is a low dam over which a river falls
do is a colloquial word for a party

explanation.surface: An odd gathering held beneath a cascade.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are informal words for an eccentric or very strange person.

clue.text: Theatrical device showing intercourse at high speed in Auden's letters

indicators.note: in places the two pieces inside the rearranged poet's name
the poet's letters are taken as a set to be reshuffled

parts.note: the poet W. H. Auden, whose surname gives its five letters
sex is intercourse
Mach one, written MACH I, is the speed of sound

explanation.surface: A racy description of fast sex in a poet's correspondence.
explanation.walkthrough: Mach one, the speed of sound, is written MACH I. 'letters' shuffles the poet's name, which the other two pieces split; 'at' and 'showing' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase, god from the machine, names a contrived plot device, originally a god lowered onto the stage.

clue.text: This writer would come back with a new chapter for very little money

indicators.note: to come back is to return, so the setter's contraction is read backwards

parts.note: the setter would is I'd

indicators.note: a new chapter is a fresh version, so the letters of chapter are rearranged

explanation.surface: An author offering a fresh chapter at a bargain price.
explanation.definitionFit: Something bought dirt-cheaply costs almost nothing, an informal intensified form of inexpensive.

clue.text: Expression of dispproval rejecting it all together

parts.note: tut is the clicking sound of disapproval

indicators.note: rejecting means sending back, so the word it is turned round

explanation.surface: Someone clicking their tongue and turning everything down.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian musical direction tells every performer to play at once, the whole ensemble.

clue.text: Evil character of compiler in the past

parts.note: the setter, who compiles the puzzle, refers to themself as I
ago means in the past

explanation.surface: The setter confessing a wicked former persona.
explanation.definitionFit: The scheming ensign in Shakespeare's Othello is one of drama's best-known villains.

clue.text: Surprised since I dropped weight first

indicators.note: first says the weight comes before the words it follows in the clue

parts.note: as can mean since, as in as it rained
a ton is a unit of weight
to shed is to drop or cast off

explanation.surface: Amazed because I shed pounds early on.
explanation.definitionFit: Being astonished is a strong synonym for being surprised or amazed.

clue.text: Right under very old-fashioned Parisian sinner

indicators.note: in a down answer, under places R below the French phrase

parts.note: a Parisian would say très passé for very old-fashioned

explanation.surface: A dated Frenchman of the right being called a sinner.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Lord's Prayer, those who trespass against us are wrongdoers, so the word means one who sins.

clue.text: See 26
Unusual pastel mural

indicators.note: unusual means out of the ordinary, so the letters of pastel take an unusual order

explanation.surface: An odd wall painting in pastels.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mural' looks like a noun but is the adjective meaning of a wall.
explanation.definitionFit: Mural as an adjective means relating to a wall, and septal describes a dividing wall or partition in anatomy.

clue.text: Most impressed with report of East End equine transport

indicators.note: a report is what is heard, so the spoken phrase is turned into a word that sounds like it

parts.note: a horse truck as a Cockney says it, dropping the h: orse truck

explanation.surface: Someone bowled over by a cockney horsebox.
explanation.walkthrough: The East End of London is Cockney territory, where the h is dropped from horse.
explanation.definitionFit: To be struck with awe is to be filled with deep wonder, a very impressed state.

clue.text: Endless bullfight or passage

indicators.note: endless means without its final letter, so the Spanish word loses its last

parts.note: corrida is the Spanish word for a bullfight

explanation.surface: A choice between a bullfight and a walkway.
explanation.definitionFit: A hallway or passage leading between rooms is a synonym in the architectural sense.

clue.text: Set off in traffic to find discarded goods

indicators.note: in puts the rearranged letters inside the traffic word

parts.note: a jam is a traffic hold-up

indicators.note: off means wrong or awry, so the letters of set are rearranged

explanation.surface: Setting off in heavy traffic and coming across dumped cargo.
explanation.definitionFit: Cargo thrown overboard to lighten a ship, which may wash ashore, is unwanted stuff cast away.

clue.text: See 9
Over-rode protective cover for missile

indicators.note: over means turned over, so the letters run backwards
the letters are concealed under cover of the words rode protective

explanation.surface: Overriding a protective covering for a rocket.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is in 'rode protective', read backwards: 'cover' signals the concealment, 'Over' the turnaround. 'for' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: An underwater self-propelled weapon launched at ships is a type of missile.

clue.text: Score with the previous clue?

definitions.meaning: a score is a set of ...
the clue before this one is number ..., the question mark flagging the whimsy

explanation.walkthrough: The clue numbered just before this one is 20, so the number names it.
explanation.definitionFit: A score means a group of twenty, and 20-down is the clue that precedes it.

clue.text: Setter would fish, being lazy

parts.note: the setter would is I'd
ling is a fish of the cod family

explanation.surface: The setter would rather go fishing than work.
explanation.definitionFit: To idle is to do nothing, so the participle means lazing about.

clue.text: Dumps containing resort communications

indicators.note: containing means holding inside, so the resort goes within the word for dumps

parts.note: to ditch is to dump
a spa is a health resort

explanation.surface: Rubbish tips at a holiday town receiving the mail.
explanation.definitionFit: Dispatches are official messages or reports sent off, a kind of communication.

clue.text: 29's partner in bad mood after Howards End

indicators.note: after puts the rearranged letters following the single letter
the end of Howards is its final letter
bad means corrupt, so the letters of mood are rearranged

explanation.surface: A grumpy reader after finishing the novel Howards End.
explanation.walkthrough: Howards End is E. M. Forster's novel; 'End' takes its last letter, S.
explanation.definitionFit: The two cities of the plain destroyed in Genesis are always named as a pair.

clue.text: See 3
3 25 crashed hired Mini into empty jukebox

indicators.note: into places the rearranged car letters inside the emptied word
an empty jukebox has lost its contents, leaving only the outer letters
a crashed car is wrecked, so the letters of hired Mini are rearranged

explanation.surface: A celebrity wrecks a rented Mini by driving into a bare jukebox.
explanation.definitionFit: The American guitarist of Purple Haze fame is a celebrated example of a rock star.

clue.text: Try to leave business for the river

indicators.note: to leave means to go away, so the word try is removed

parts.note: industry is business activity
try taken as written

explanation.surface: Quitting the business world for a life by the water.
explanation.definitionFit: The great river of Pakistan, flowing from Tibet into the Arabian Sea.

clue.text: Becoming interested during tie break

indicators.note: to break is to smash apart, so the letters of during tie are rearranged

explanation.surface: A spectator getting hooked during a tie-break in tennis.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tie break' looks like the tennis term; 'break' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Intrigued describes curiosity being aroused, a state of becoming interested.

clue.text: God's mortal rage, He half visited on this place

indicators.note: half of each word is its first half, so each of the four words gives its opening half

explanation.surface: Divine fury visited on a sinful city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half' takes GO, MOR, RA and H; 'visited on' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The biblical city destroyed by fire and brimstone is the place on which God's wrath fell.

clue.text: Watch the heart

definitions.meaning: a timepiece, informally named for its ticking
slang for the heart, which beats like a clock

explanation.definitionFit: Both a wristwatch and the heart are informally called by this name because they tick.
